messages:
Jordan: Handoff — quick FYI before I go offline in 10. We started seeing a small uptick in generation latency alerts for hosted-prod (~p50 moved from 110ms -> 240ms). I adjusted the alert thresholds temporarily to avoid paging on noisy short spikes while we investigate. Details below.

Jordan: TL;DR: temporarily raised the latency alert from 200ms -> 350ms for route /v1/generate for the next 45m, suppressed duplicate alerts for 5m, kept error-rate and outage paging unchanged. I'm primary for the next 10 min then handing to Alex as secondary.

Alex: ack. can you paste the exact PD policy change and runbook pointer? want to make sure paging behavior is what i expect.

Jordan: yes — PD change id `PD-4821-temp-routing`. Escalation stays same (primary -> secondary -> oncall-lead). I ran the suppression via our alert-manager UI, command shown: 

```
# temporary suppression
alertmanagerctl silence --match 'route="/v1/generate" severity=latency' --duration=5m --reason 'handoff temp threshold tweak'
```

Jordan: runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/latency-investigation (see step 2 for quick KV cache sanity checks). Also check the model-variant fallback logs at `prod/serve/fallbacks` if you see sudden p99 spikes.

Priya: noted. do we know if this was capacity-related (burst) or a routing policy flake? I can check router logs — grabbing ASG and pod metrics now.

incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert triggered: latency_high /v1/generate (p50=238ms, p95=520ms) — 3 occurrences in last 3m — alert id 87321 — routed to eng-oncall.

Sam: seeing a small surge from eu-west-1 -> increased model load on instances with quantized models. Might be a traffic shift from a customer experiment. No errors, just latency.

Alex: thanks. If it's a traffic shift, we should avoid paging unless error-rate increases. Good call to raise threshold. Can you confirm the suppression won't hide real outages?

Jordan: suppression is scoped: only latency severity for route /v1/generate; error-rate and 5xx have full paging. Also I left a high-sev fallback: if p50>1s or p95>1.5s then immediate PD page (severity=critical). That is unchanged.

Priya: checking router logs now — quick grep shows increased host connections to variant `gpt-small-q4_0` with concurrent streams up ~2.2x in last 6m. Looks like customer A running a batch job. Not seeing any KV cache evictions.

Alex: ok — mitigation options: 1) throttle the customer at edge (rate-limit header), 2) spin up a few more capacity units in eu-west pool, 3) route lower-priority traffic to cheaper variant. Which do we prefer right now?

Sam: I'd opt for (2) short-term autoscale; takes ~60s to add one GPU instance. (1) is quick but could impact their job. (3) requires routing rules change and might need a canary.

Jordan: I kicked an autoscale request: `infractl scale pool eu-west-1 --add 1 --reason 'latency spike'` — should be up in ~90s.

incident-bot: infra job 9923 started: scale request accepted.

Alex: good. keep an eye on p95. If no improvement in 3m, we throttle the offending token prefix via edge policy. Also let's document the temporary SLO note so ops and customers are aware.

Jordan: added temporary SLO note to internal status page: "Latency threshold for /v1/generate temporarily raised to 350ms from 200ms while we investigate traffic spike — no customer-facing SLA change; pages only on high-sev errors." link: https://status.redwood.internal/notes/1812345678

Priya: autoscale completed — new instance attached to eu-west pool, warming caches. p95 dropped from 520ms -> 180ms within one minute. Nice.

Alex: great! Can we remove suppression and restore original threshold now? want to avoid hiding further regressions.

Jordan: I'll restore in 2m once metrics steady for 1m. Restoring with: 

```
alertmanagerctl update-threshold --route '/v1/generate' --metric p50 --threshold 200ms
alertmanagerctl silence --remove 'handoff temp threshold tweak'
```

incident-bot: metrics update: p95=175ms, p50=95ms.

Jordan: restored thresholds and removed suppression. PD policy back to normal.

Alex: thanks. quick post-handoff checklist: 1) Priya — note the autoscale cause in the incident entry, 2) Jordan — include the temporary threshold change in the handoff notes, 3) Sam — follow up with capacity team about pre-warming for customer A if they plan repeated runs.

Priya: will add note to incident ticket: INC-2026-881 with logs and grep output.

Sam: will reach out to capacity; flagged customer A for potential scheduled batch.

Jordan: handing off now — Alex you're primary, Sam secondary for the next 4h. I'm available on DM for 30 more mins. Good luck :thumbsup:

Alex: taking over. thanks Jordan. ping me if it regresses.

Priya: thanks, gl.

incident-bot: Thread closed by Jordan — handoff complete."
